vulnerabilities.description: PCRE2 before 10.48 allows a pcre2_dfa_match out-of-bounds write because reuse of a cached workspace block, in a recursive DFA matching workspace, lacks a size check (even though a newly allocated block, for the same purpose, does have a size check). This outcome requires an attacker-controlled regular expression, or a recursive pattern in conjunction with a small heap limit (this can be set through the API).
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not link or invoke native libpcre2.

ratings.justification: Liquibase is a pure-Java application (java.util.regex) with no linkage to native libpcre2, and docker-entrypoint.sh performs no regex or grep operations.

analysis.detail: PCRE2 pcre2_dfa_match out-of-bounds write via cached workspace reuse, fixed upstream in PCRE2 10.48 but not yet backported to Ubuntu noble. Liquibase is a pure-Java application (java.util.regex) with no linkage to native libpcre2, and docker-entrypoint.sh performs no regex or grep operations.

vulnerabilities.description: PCRE2 before 10.49, when there is an attacker-controlled regular expression and certain JIT API usage, allows an out-of-bounds write with arbitrary data.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. No shipped program compiles externally supplied patterns with the PCRE2 JIT.

ratings.justification: The vulnerable JIT path needs an attacker-controlled pattern and a caller-managed JIT stack; only grep -P qualifies and nothing in the image runs it.

analysis.detail: Triggering the out-of-bounds write needs three things at once: JIT compilation, an application-created growable JIT stack assigned with pcre2_jit_stack_assign, and an attacker-controlled pattern with a very large number of capturing groups. In the image only GNU grep in -P mode uses that API, and nothing runs grep at runtime: the entrypoint calls ls, touch, rm, tr and env with fixed arguments, Liquibase evaluates regular expressions with java.util.regex, lpm is a static Go binary, and libselinux (the other pcre2 consumer, loaded by coreutils) compiles no patterns without an SELinux policy. No changelog, SQL, database response, argument or environment value ever becomes a pcre2 pattern.
